Physics hand-checked: the three basic methods are amplitude modulation (AM), frequency modulation (FM) and phase modulation (PM) — the book misprints the third abbreviation as '(FM)'; this card corrects it to (PM).

recall_prompt: Name the three basic methods of modulation with their abbreviations, and say which property of the carrier each one varies.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three methods named
lines: There are three basic methods of
steps.margin_note: First mark. All three names with their abbreviations AM, FM and PM — the book misprints the third abbreviation as FM.
steps.why: A carrier wave has exactly three properties that can be varied — amplitude, frequency and phase — so there are exactly three basic methods, one per property. The book prints 'iii) phase modulation (FM)': a misprint. The abbreviation for phase modulation is PM; FM is frequency modulation.
common_mistakes: Copying the book's '(FM)' for phase modulation. Phase modulation is PM.
Naming only AM and FM. Phase modulation is the third basic method.

recall.must_convey: That the three basic methods are amplitude modulation (AM), frequency modulation (FM) and phase modulation (PM).
accept: the three are AM FM PM
reject: the amplitude of the carrier is varied

steps.memory_tip: Each abbreviation is the first letter of what changes: A for amplitude, F for frequency, P for phase.

steps.label: What each method varies
lines: In each method, one property of the
to the message signal: its amplitude in AM,
its frequency in FM, and its phase in PM.

lines.text: AM: amplitude · FM: frequency · PM: phase

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Match each method to the one property it varies.
steps.why: Naming the methods is memory; saying what each one varies shows the idea — the message is written onto the carrier by changing exactly one of the carrier's three properties.
common_mistakes: Saying AM varies the message signal's amplitude. It varies the CARRIER's amplitude according to the message.
Mixing the pairs — FM varies frequency, PM varies phase, never the other way around.

recall.must_convey: That AM varies the carrier's amplitude, FM its frequency and PM its phase, in each case according to the message signal.
accept: one property of the carrier per method

steps.memory_tip: Three properties of a wave, three methods — the name of the method tells you the property it varies.

insider_note: The book prints phase modulation as (FM); write (PM). First mark is the three names, second is the property each varies — the abbreviation already encodes it.
